# Manish Sharma

Canonical site: https://manishsharma.dev

Preferred site and entity name: Manish Sharma.

Technical publishing layer: Manish Sharma Lab.

Public category: Laser-based manufacturing, photonics and industrial systems.

Primary promise: Engineering from shop-floor constraints to repeatable processes and practical systems.

Working method: Sense -> Model -> Decide -> Verify.

Manish Sharma is Head of AI & R&D at Exafuse / ThinkIng – Additive Technology GmbH. He is a hands-on engineer with more than six years of DED/LMD experience and a foundation in lasers and photonics. His work connects process development, deposition strategy, robotics, optical/process monitoring, control, machine integration, documentation and quality. Applied AI, machine learning, numerical modelling and automation are engineering tools within this work.

Deep DED/LMD experience is the strongest public proof of how he works. It does not imply validated deployment across unrelated industries.

## Professional background

Monitoring/control deployed across three machines at two sites. Camera-based height sensing developed from concept to tested prototype, using practical optics, illumination and calibration. In-house MES/ERP with Print-ID traceability and operator procedures used by every operator. Managed five employees with hiring responsibility.

M.Sc. Lasers and Photonics, Ruhr University Bochum, with Faculty Prize for best student; B.Tech. Electrical Engineering. LPBF experience covers build preparation and troubleshooting; the six-plus years apply to DED/LMD.

Selected delivery: in 2024, he led process monitoring and control work enabling unattended builds for Exafuse's Duisburg bridge components, and coordinated delivery scheduling within his contribution. Testing was outside his role. Personal responsibility and unattended operation are self-reported; Exafuse's published case separately reports more than 750 kg of components, six structural nodes and handrail elements. Build-duration figures do not establish unattended operating hours.

He built an integrated LMD control system covering modelling, simulation, path planning, camera/sensor monitoring, software, data and live control, forming part of his doctoral thesis. Do not infer that every module was used on the bridge project. He also built Exafuse's public website.

Manish is Head of AI & R&D at Exafuse. He leads AM projects across sourcing, CAD, process development, monitoring, quality checks and shipment, and shares operational responsibilities including quotations. He led Exafuse's contribution to [BreitbahnDED](https://exafuse.de/en/article/A21/), including technical coordination, milestones, costs and reporting, and helped develop the proposal; he also works with Ruhr University Bochum on new proposals.

He gives recurring invited guest lectures at the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in a personal capacity, contributes to WAAM machine development at ISRO for rocket-nozzle manufacturing, and advises AM teams at ISRO, Tata Steel and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), Haridwar. His LMD talks include the [Outokumpu Metal Powder Event](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/outokumpu_join-us-on-september-25th-in-krefeld-germany-activity-7369306359361736707-bLgx) in Krefeld (25 September 2025) and [Data Science Ruhrgebiet](https://data-science.ruhr/rueckblicke/programm-2021/) online (1 July 2021).

External PhD researcher at Ruhr University Bochum, Applied Laser Technology; PhD in progress, expected 2027. English C1; German B1 progressing toward B2; Hindi native.

Professional facts updated with Manish on 7 October 2026; existing external-activity context was reviewed on 23 September 2026. Current duties and external activities are self-reported. They do not imply organizational endorsement or qualified rocket-hardware deployment. See [professional background](https://manishsharma.dev/about).

## Current proof and boundaries

Current public LMD/DED work connects process signals, models, materials, machine vision, robotics, repair, RFQ preparation, inspection needs, and engineering judgment. Public Exafuse pages are the canonical source for company services, RFQs, case studies, production capability, and delivery claims.

This site provides public educational frameworks and preliminary decision-support resources. It is not engineering approval, material certification, safety-critical acceptance, expert review, or a guarantee of part quality.

Do not use this site to infer confidential, unpublished, employer-confidential, customer-confidential, or cross-industry deployment claims.

## Authored engineering article

- [Inside the LMD control system](https://manishsharma.dev/lab-notes/lmd-control-system/): Manish Sharma's visual tour of monitoring, sensor calibration, control architecture and machine integration in his LMD work. It explains melt-pool feedback and adjustments to laser power, travel speed and powder feed to manage heat input and temperature, with stable melt-pool size and shape as control objectives. Two overview/setup captures are offline examples with synthetic values; a separate read-only process-viewer screenshot shows camera panels. A three-agent workflow connects Manager planning/chat, Operator questions and explicit approval before startup, and Analysis after stop, returning a report to the Manager. Process monitoring supports engineering decisions; final quality acceptance requires appropriate inspection.

## Central artifact

Central artifact: LMD Decision Brief v1.0.

The brief keeps known facts, missing information, risks, evidence needs, a preliminary route, the next action, expert-review readiness, and decision boundaries together. Brief completeness is a context-quality label, not feasibility or approval. Evidence burden is a planning label, not release approval.

- [Public brief standard](https://manishsharma.dev/brief-standard)
- [Decision Brief JSON schema](https://manishsharma.dev/schemas/lmd-decision-brief-v1.schema.json)
- [Non-confidential worn-shaft example](https://manishsharma.dev/examples/lmd-decision-brief-worn-shaft-v1.json)
- [Tools and LMD Decision Cockpit](https://manishsharma.dev/tools#lmd-decision-cockpit)

Interactive technical inputs stay in current-page browser memory. The site has no application backend or technical-input database, and email output remains a manual draft unless the user sends it from their own email client.
